title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes study the boundary structure ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν}, that is, the Deligne–Mumford compactification stratified by combinatorial type.

On the previous page, Grothendieck has a nodal curve X̂ with normalization Y (later written X̃^ or Ŷ). He sets:
- S = π_0(Y), the components of the normalization;
- Ã = the preimages in Y of the double points;
- A = Sing(X̂), with Ã → A of degree 2 defining a fixed-point-free involution σ_Ã;
- σ: Ã → S, the 'origin' map.
This is a graph in Serre's sense (vertices S, oriented edges Ã, reversal involution). The marked points I ⊂ X̂(k) give an extra map I → S.

This page interprets the data geometrically:
- Vertices are the irreducible components X_α.
- Unoriented edges are the double points (ordinary quadratic singularities). An edge joins α and β when the node lies on X_α ∩ X_β.
- Closed loops at α correspond bijectively to the double points of X_α itself. Hence 'all X_α smooth' is equivalent to 'G_X has no loops', i.e. the origin of each edge differs from its endpoint.

The page then begins a realizability claim. Every finite graph, up to isomorphism, arises from a suitable X̂. Continuing on the next page, one can moreover prescribe the genera g_α of the normalized components and a map I → S realized by smooth marked points. This leads to the definition of the 'maquette' of a stable curve: the triple (graph G_X, I → S, genus function g: S → ℕ). In modern terms this is a stable or modular graph (dual graph of a stable marked curve).
errors: Realizability: 'tout graphe fini peut être obtenu' requires the graph to be connected if X̂ is meant to be connected, as a stable curve is. Arbitrary finite graphs are realized only by possibly disconnected nodal curves.
Realizability with marked points also requires a base field with enough rational points, e.g. k algebraically closed, so that distinct smooth points can be chosen on each component.

If X is to be stable, the realizable maquettes are only those satisfying the stability inequality 2g_α − 2 + n_α > 0 at each vertex, where n_α counts half-edges plus markings. This is not stated here, though it may be addressed later.

Minor bookkeeping: with Ã the set of oriented edges, a loop at α contributes two arcs but corresponds to one double point. The bijection holds with unoriented edges, as intended. (The next page's 'Ã = Sing(X)' appears to conflate Ã with A.)

ideas.what: Dual graph of a nodal curve: components as vertices, nodes as edges, self-nodes as loops; smooth components iff no loops
ideas.modern_name: dual graph of a nodal/stable curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; Deligne–Mumford (1969) era, systematized in boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} (Knudsen, later Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} but not this explicit formalism, to my knowledge

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard description of the dual graph of a nodal curve and the start of the definition of the 'stable graph' (Grothendieck's 'maquette'). The only idiosyncrasy is the terminology 'maquette'. The mathematics is textbook material for the boundary of M̄_{g,n}.
